metaDescription: Chinese Shar-Pei vaccine schedule with core ages in weeks. Set reminders so Chinese Shar-Pei boosters are not missed.

bodySections.heading: Why timing matters for this schedule
paragraphs: The Chinese Shar-Pei core series (DA2PP / DHPP plus rabies per law) is plotted at 8, 12, 16, 16 weeks in the table above so a medium puppy is covered as maternal antibodies fade.
At 45-60 lb (20-27 kg), Chinese Shar-Pei visit logistics matter as much as antigens: book the 16-week appointment before class, daycare, or boarding asks for proof.
Bring familial shar-pei fever risk and skin fold infections into the Chinese Shar-Pei exam-room conversation while you are already there for shots.
Rabies for a Chinese Shar-Pei still follows local statute, and when the clinic allows you can pair it with the ≥16-week core finish, then photograph the certificate into PetClues the same day.

bodySections.heading: If a dose is missed or delayed
paragraphs: Owners postpone Chinese Shar-Pei shots when the puppy seems “a little off,” travel intervenes, or familial shar-pei fever risk worries dominate the week — ask the clinic whether a same-week Chinese Shar-Pei make-up is still appropriate instead of sliding to the annual exam.
Long gaps can leave Chinese Shar-Pei antibody levels uncertain, so expect either an added booster or a titer conversation rather than a shrug.
Do not trade the missed Chinese Shar-Pei dose for extra socialization; finish immunity first for this medium dog.
Reset the Chinese Shar-Pei reminder stack the evening of the make-up appointment — including the eventual adult booster after the 16-week finish.

faqs.question: When does the Chinese Shar-Pei core vaccine series usually finish?
faqs.answer: This breed record completes core vaccines around 16 weeks of age, with rabies timed per local law. Your clinic may adjust intervals for the individual puppy.

faqs.question: What should I do if my Chinese Shar-Pei misses a booster?
faqs.answer: Contact your veterinarian for a catch-up plan instead of restarting or skipping ahead. Keep prior dates handy and limit high-risk exposure until the series is current again.

faqs.question: Where can I read Chinese Shar-Pei health context beyond vaccines?
faqs.answer: See the Chinese Shar-Pei adult health guide for breed predispositions such as familial shar-pei fever risk, then bring those notes to wellness and vaccine visits.
